lines.text: Mickey Mouse's watch rescued a clockmaker.
In the Great Depression, a Connecticut clock company was near bankruptcy.
Disney's licensing agent Kay Kamen arranged a Mickey Mouse watch.
The company sold it under the Ingersoll name.
The watch debuted at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair.

post.caption: Mickey Mouse's watch rescued a clockmaker. In the Great Depression, a Connecticut clock company was near bankruptcy. Disney's licensing agent Kay Kamen arranged a Mickey Mouse watch with it, and the watch debuted at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair. Walt Disney reportedly thought it would never sell. On one day at Macy's in New York it sold 11,000 watches, and more than two million sold in about two years. The hit rescued the company and brought money to Disney. In 1957, Walt Disney was handed the 25 millionth watch.
